name: Design-Build vs Separate Designer and Contractor

mainEntity.name: Should I choose design-build or separate designer and contractor for an ADU project?
mainEntity.text: Should I choose design-build or separate designer and contractor for an ADU project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Design-build and separate designer-plus-contractor models both work, but they solve different problems. Design-build is often appealing for ADUs and custom remodels because the team can align feasibility, cost, and constructability from the start. That can reduce redesigns and make permitting smoother. A separate designer and contractor arrangement may provide more independent design creativity, but it also requires stronger communication and more project oversight. For homeowners with limited time or a complex site, design-build can simplify decision-making. For highly customized architectural goals, separate teams may be preferred. The right answer depends on how much coordination the homeowner wants to manage and how critical early budget control is to the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design-build can be more efficient because design and construction are coordinated under one team, which can reduce handoff errors and redesign costs. Separate designer and contractor arrangements may offer more flexibility but can require more coordination from the homeowner. The best choice depends on project complexity, budget control, and how much management you want to handle.
